traceability.evidence:
1) Implementation file: src/rules/valid-req-reference.ts - JSDoc header explicitly ties the rule to this story and its deep-validation requirements: * @story docs/stories/010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION.story.md * @req REQ-DEEP-PARSE, REQ-DEEP-MATCH, REQ-DEEP-CACHE, REQ-DEEP-PATH - Core behavior in validateReqLine({...}): * Extracts requirement ID from @req line: const parts = line.split(/\s+/); const reqId = parts[1]. * Validates storyPath against path traversal and absolute paths; on invalid paths it calls context.report({ messageId: "invalidPath", data: { storyPath } }). * Resolves the story file path with path.resolve(cwd, storyPath) and ensures it stays within the project directory. * Caches parsed requirements per story file: uses a Map<string, Set> reqCache keyed by resolvedStoryPath; if a path is not in the cache, it reads the file once with fs.readFileSync and parses all occurrences of the regex /REQ-[A-Z0-9-]+/g into the Set, then reuses that Set for subsequent validations (REQ-DEEP-PARSE, REQ-DEEP-CACHE). * If reading the file fails (e.g., missing or malformed), it catches the error and stores an empty Set, avoiding crashes and still allowing linting to proceed (graceful error handling). * If the referenced reqId is not found in the Set, it reports context.report({ messageId: "reqMissing", data: { reqId, storyPath } }), providing clear, requirement-specific diagnostics (REQ-DEEP-MATCH, REQ-DEEP-ERROR). - Comment/annotation integration: * extractStoryPath(comment) scans JSDoc lines for "@story" and returns the referenced story path, satisfying REQ-DEEP-PARSE for annotations. * handleAnnotationLine(...) dispatches @story and @req lines; for @req it calls validateReqLine, integrating with existing annotation parsing logic. * handleComment(...) iterates lines in a comment block, updating storyPath as it encounters @story and @req, reusing the last storyPath as context. * programListener(context) builds a Program visitor that collects all comments via context.getSourceCode().getAllComments(), then calls handleComment for each; it also owns and shares the reqCache Map across all comments for that file, implementing in-run caching. - Error messages (user experience): * meta.messages.reqMissing: "Requirement '{{reqId}}' not found in '{{storyPath}}'" – includes both missing requirement ID and story path, matching REQ-DEEP-ERROR and 007.0-DEV-ERROR-REPORTING. * meta.messages.invalidPath: "Invalid story path '{{storyPath}}'" – clearly identifies invalid story path issues for @req/@story combos. - Implicit support for multiple formats and sections: * Because the regex /REQ-[A-Z0-9-]+/g is run over the entire file content, any occurrence of a REQ-... token in headings, paragraphs, bullet lists, checkboxes, or numbered lists is recognized. This satisfies handling of different story structures and requirement formats at the behavior level, even without a full markdown AST.
2) Tests: tests/rules/valid-req-reference.test.ts - File header explicitly references this story and the deep-validation requirement: * "Tests for: docs/stories/010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION.story.md" * @story docs/stories/010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION.story.md * @req REQ-DEEP-PARSE and references to 007.0-DEV-ERROR-REPORTING requirements for error behavior. - Uses ESLint RuleTester to validate behavior: * Valid cases: - Case "[REQ-DEEP-PARSE] valid requirement reference existing in story file" with code: // @story docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md // @req REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE This proves that the rule successfully finds REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE inside docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md. - Case "[REQ-DEEP-BULLET] valid bullet list requirement existing in bullet story fixture" with code: // @story tests/fixtures/story_bullet.md // @req REQ-BULLET-LIST backed by tests/fixtures/story_bullet.md, which contains: - REQ-BULLET-LIST - a requirement in bullet list format This demonstrates correct handling of bullet-list requirement formats. * Invalid cases (error handling and messages): - "[REQ-DEEP-MATCH] missing requirement in story file": code uses @req REQ-NON-EXISTENT against docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md and expects an error with messageId "reqMissing" and data { reqId: "REQ-NON-EXISTENT", storyPath: "docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md" }. - "[REQ-DEEP-PARSE] disallow path traversal in story path": code uses story path "../docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md" and expects messageId "invalidPath" with the same storyPath, verifying invalid-path detection. - "[REQ-DEEP-PARSE] disallow absolute path in story path": code uses an absolute path and expects messageId "invalidPath" again. - "[REQ-DEEP-BULLET] missing bullet list requirement in bullet story fixture": code uses @req REQ-MISSING-BULLET against tests/fixtures/story_bullet.md and expects messageId "reqMissing" with the correct reqId and storyPath. - The describe block title explicitly references the story: "Valid Req Reference Rule (Story 010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION)", maintaining traceability.
3) Story and fixture content - docs/stories/010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION.story.md exists and defines: * Requirements: REQ-DEEP-PARSE, REQ-DEEP-MATCH, REQ-DEEP-FORMAT, REQ-DEEP-SECTION, REQ-DEEP-CACHE, REQ-DEEP-ERROR. * Acceptance criteria covering core functionality, quality, integration with existing logic, user experience, error handling, and documentation. - docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md exists and defines REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE and related REQ-... IDs used in tests as real-world story data. - tests/fixtures/story_bullet.md contains bullet-formatted requirement IDs (e.g., "- REQ-BULLET-LIST - a requirement in bullet list format"), which are correctly recognized by the rule, demonstrating handling of non-trivial markdown structures.
4) Documentation - docs/rules/valid-req-reference.md: * Describes the rule as: "Enforces that `@req` annotations reference existing requirements in story files and protects against invalid paths." * Annotated with @story docs/stories/010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION.story.md and @req REQ-DEEP-PARSE, REQ-DEEP-MATCH, REQ-DEEP-PATH. * Explains behaviors that match the story’s acceptance criteria: validating paths, parsing story files for requirement IDs, matching @req against those IDs, and reporting both invalidPath and reqMissing errors. * Includes concrete code examples for correct usage, missing requirements, and invalid paths.
5) Plugin integration and tests execution - src/index.ts includes "valid-req-reference" in RULE_NAMES and exports it via the plugin’s rules map; both "recommended" and "strict" configs enable "traceability/valid-req-reference": "error", so the deep-validation behavior is active when the plugin is used. - jest.config.js is configured to run tests from tests/**/*.test.ts using ts-jest; the project test suite includes tests/rules/valid-req-reference.test.ts which directly covers this story. - Test command used: "npm test -- --verbose" which runs "jest --ci --bail --verbose" without any reported failures, indicating that the valid-req-reference rule tests pass under the configured Jest environment.
traceability.notes: The ESLint rule traceability/valid-req-reference, its tests, and its documentation collectively implement the deep requirement content validation described in docs/stories/010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION.story.md. The rule parses story files to find requirement IDs, validates each @req annotation against those IDs, caches parsed content per story file within a lint run, blocks unsafe story paths, and produces clear, specific error messages when requirements are missing or paths are invalid. Tests cover both successful matches and error scenarios (including bullet-list-formatted requirements), and user-facing documentation explains usage and behavior with examples. This satisfies the story’s core functionality, quality, integration, user-experience, error-handling, and documentation acceptance criteria.
